Strengths: Simple & Interpretable – easy to understand, explain, and implement.
Weaknesses: Linearity Assumption – cannot capture complex, non-linear patterns unless you add transformations.

Strengths: Computationally Efficient – very fast to train, even on large datasets.
Weaknesses: Sensitive to Outliers – a single extreme value can distort coefficients and predictions.

Strengths: Provides Feature Importance – coefficients show influence of predictors.
Weaknesses: Multicollinearity Problem – highly correlated predictors make coefficients unstable and hard to interpret.

Strengths: Statistical Inference – supports confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, and p-values.
Weaknesses: Assumptions Must Hold – violations (non-normal errors, heteroscedasticity, dependence) lead to unreliable results.

Strengths: Works Well with Linear Relationships – gives unbiased and efficient estimates when assumptions are satisfied.
Weaknesses: Limited Expressiveness – can only naturally model additive, linear effects (no thresholds or complex interactions unless added manually).

Strengths: Extensible – can add polynomial/interaction terms or use regularization (Ridge/Lasso).
Weaknesses: Extrapolation Risk – predictions outside training range are unreliable.

Strengths: Good Baseline Model – useful starting point before applying complex ML models.
Weaknesses: Not Robust for High Dimensions – overfits when predictors >> observations unless regularized.

Strengths: Interpretability Matters – often used in economics, healthcare, and social sciences.
Weaknesses: Not Suitable for Complex Data Types – cannot handle images, text, or sequences without preprocessing.
